html:
The map's name, in 1880 and 1900, for the kingdom ruled from Antananarivo by the Merina people of the central highlands, which by then controlled most of Madagascar. The longer history of the kingdom is told under Merina Kingdom.

King Andrianampoinimerina reunited Imerina around 1800, and his son Radama I conquered much of the island with British help. Queen Ranavalona I expelled the missionaries and persecuted Christians, but in 1869 the court converted to Protestant Christianity. From 1864 to 1895 the real ruler was the prime minister Rainilaiarivony, who married three queens in turn and modernised the army, schools and laws.

France invaded in 1883 and imposed a protectorate in 1885. A second invasion in 1895 took Antananarivo. In 1897 France abolished the monarchy and sent Queen Ranavalona III into exile, and the island became French Madagascar.
